Stage 4 · Perfect?

Perfect?

I have done it — or I did it last year?
Track 12.12 — eight sentencesOriginal coursebook recording
Show transcript
1 I opened the door. 2 I've opened the door. 3 She's run a marathon. 4 She ran a marathon. 5 We've met him. 6 We met him. 7 I've watched Star Wars twice this month. 8 I watched Star Wars twice last month.
11 — “I opened the door.” is…
23 — “She's run a marathon.” is…
35 — “We've met him.” is…
48 — “…twice last month.” is…
Why

Listen for 've / 's and run/met — and for the time words: this month (perfect) vs last month (past).

In other words
“Have you visited Brazil before?” — “Yes, I have — twice.”
“I came here when I was a child.”
“I've never been here before.”
“I was here three years ago for work.”
Notice

Notice: the same trip, two tenses. What do “when I was a child” and “three years ago” change?

Present Perfect — life, no timePast Simple — a finished time
ExampleI've visited Brazil twice.I came here when I was a child.
QuestionHave you ever been to Rio?Did you go to Rio last year?
Time wordsever · never · before · twice · this monthyesterday · last week · in 2010 · ago · when I was…
The cluelisten for 've / 's and run/seen/beenlisten for ran/saw/was and the time
In other words
Experience, no time → Present Perfect: I've been to Rio.
A finished time (ago, last week, in 2010, when I was…) → Past Simple: I went to Rio in 2015.
They work together: “Have you visited Brazil? — Yes. I came here as a child.”
Stage 5 · Clinic

Clinic

Six mistakes from the whole course. Beat them one last time.
1❌ “She have won many prizes.”
2❌ “Did you went to the festival?”
3❌ “I'm knowing the answer.”
4❌ “There is many cafés in Rio.”
5❌ “He don't work on Sundays.”
6❌ “Rio is more hotter than London.”
Why

has won · Did you go · know (state verb) · there are a lot of · doesn't work · hotter.

Stage 6 · Rio

Rio

Two film stars at the Rio festival — both tenses in one interview.

Listen once. Then choose the correct answers.

Track 12.11 — Pavel and Wanda in RioOriginal coursebook recording
Show transcript
I: So Pavel, you're here for the Rio de Janeiro film festival. Have you visited Brazil before? P: Yes, I have — twice. Actually, I came here when I was a child, and I was here three years ago for work, too. I: And what about you, Wanda? Have you ever been to Rio before? W: No, I've never been here before, but it's a beautiful city. I: I saw your latest film Inbox Me last night and I thought it was really wonderful. P: Well, thank you very much! I: And everyone else in the cinema enjoyed it, too. When it finished, people stood up and clapped! P: Really? I'm delighted. A lot of people have said some lovely things about it. W: Last week someone told me it was their favourite film of the year!
1Has Pavel visited Brazil before?
2When did he come here first?
3Has Wanda been to Rio before?
4What happened when the film finished?
Why

Twice — as a child and three years ago (Past Simple for the times!). Wanda — never. And the cinema stood up and clapped.

Stage 7 · The call

The call

The final skill: a phone call in English.

Listen once. Then choose the correct answers.

Track 12.16 — two calls about one showOriginal coursebook recording
Show transcript
F: Hello? M: Hi Francis, it's Marcus. Is Caitlin there? F: She's not here at the moment. M: Can you tell her to call me back, please? F: Oh wait, she's just come back. Hang on a minute. I'll just get her. C: Hi, Marcus. M: Have you booked tickets for the comedy club tonight? C: No, I haven't. Their website said they're sold out. M: Why don't you call them and ask about returned tickets? C: Good idea! I'll call them now. — R: Good afternoon. Phoenix Comedy Club. How can I help you? C: Hello. Could I speak to the ticket office manager, please? R: I'm afraid he's not available at the moment. Can I help? C: I'm calling about the show tonight. Has anyone returned any tickets? R: I'm not sure — you'll need to speak to the manager. C: Could you ask him to call me back, please? R: Yes, of course. Could I have your number, please?
1Has Caitlin booked the tickets?
2What is Marcus's idea?
3Is the ticket office manager available?
Why

Sold out online · but people return tickets · the manager isn't available — “Could you ask him to call me back?”

Track 12.17 — the phone phrasesOriginal coursebook recording
Show transcript
1 Hi Francis, it's Marcus. Is Caitlin there? 2 Hello. Could I speak to the ticket office manager, please? 3 She's not here at the moment. 4 I'm afraid he's not available at the moment. 5 Can you tell her to call me back, please? 6 Could you ask him to call me back, please? 7 Could I have your number, please? 8 Hang on a minute. I'll just get her.
Track 12.18 — a 20-second callOriginal coursebook recording
Show transcript
A: Right Insurance. How can I help you? B: Hello. Could I speak to Ms Martinez, please? A: One moment, please. I'm afraid she's out of the office at the moment. Would you like to leave a message? B: No, that's fine. I'll call back later. A: OK, thank you. B: Thanks. Bye.
1“Would you like to leave a message?” — he says:
Why

“I'll call back later.” — short, polite, perfect.

Notice

Next level preview: at Pre-Intermediate you'll meet sentences like “She was working when I called.” Just say hello to it — no need to use it yet.

Stage 8 · Write

Write

Write “My year in English” — with every tense you own.

6–8 sentences: past, present, experience and plans.

Useful language
  • When I started, I was… / I couldn't…
  • In Lesson … I learnt…
  • Now I can… / I usually…
  • I've written… / I've never…
  • Next year I'm going to…
  • The best lesson was…
One phone call, one interview — everything you know.

Then swap roles.

Useful language
  • Could I speak to…?
  • I'm afraid… / One moment, please
  • Have you ever…?
  • When did you…?
  • What are you going to do next year?
  • I've… and I'm going to…
One phone call, one interview — everything you know.

Then swap roles.

Useful language
  • Could I speak to…?
  • I'm afraid… / One moment, please
  • Have you ever…?
  • When did you…?
  • What are you going to do next year?
  • I've… and I'm going to…
In other words
Scene 1 — the call. Student A phones Student B's “office”. B answers like a receptionist (One moment, please… I'm afraid…). A asks to speak to someone, leaves a message, arranges a meeting time.
Scene 2 — the interview. At the meeting, B interviews A about their whole year: their story (past), their routine (present), what they have done (perfect), their plans (going to).
Swap — and make the second run faster and braver.

Stage 9 · Verbs

Verbs

The top 25 irregular verbs — know all three forms before Pre-Intermediate.

Tap a card: base form → Past Simple → Past Participle. It speaks when it flips.

In other words
💡 Say each chain out loud three times: go — went — gone. The middle form is your Past Simple (I went); the last form works with have for the Present Perfect (I've gone).
Stage 10 · Type it

Type it

Now produce it — type, don’t tap.

Spelling counts. Type the answers, then check.

1___ you ever been to Rio?
2I ___ the film last week. (see \u2192 past)
3I'm ___ to call back later.
Why

Last week \u2192 Past Simple \u00b7 ever \u2192 Present Perfect \u00b7 Could I speak to\u2026, please?

1I've saw it twice.
2Could I to speak to the manager?
3She don't available.
Why

Last week \u2192 Past Simple \u00b7 ever \u2192 Present Perfect \u00b7 Could I speak to\u2026, please?

1Finished time \u2192 past: I see the film. (last week)
2Experience \u2192 perfect: you / ever / be to Rio
3On the phone \u2014 ask for Ms Lee.
Why

Last week \u2192 Past Simple \u00b7 ever \u2192 Present Perfect \u00b7 Could I speak to\u2026, please?
